svg.title: How IntentOS works, from onboarding to the merge gate and the guardian
svg.desc: Three lanes: people, the IntentOS plugin, and model threads, over a band of trusted state. Onboard indexes the repository; a mining model proposes rules from an evidence digest, IntentOS checks each reference and runs each test, and the ones that pass are written into the policy; a person can review and edit them, but does not have to. For each ticket a QA thread fills the gaps the repository can answer, flags contradictions with the policy and sends the remaining questions back to the team; once the ticket is ready, a planner proposes a contract the compiler validates, an implementer works in a git worktree, verification runs hidden tests and deterministic checks from a snapshot with bounded repairs, the merge gate requires approvals, CI, a sync check and merged-result verification before fast-forwarding main, and the guardian bisects a red main and opens a validated undo PR.
svg.text: Learn the repository · once, then per revision
verification, the gate and the guardian are deterministic code
outside the repository · written only by IntentOS after its checks
policy YAML: invariants · architecture rules · decisions
